solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tumble from branch

definitions.meaning: to tumble to something is British slang for realising or catching on to it
a small shoot or slender branch of a tree or shrub

explanation.surface: Something falls out of a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: the slang verb meaning to grasp or understand, and the noun for a small woody shoot.

clue.text: Wife has to vomit, poor devil

parts.note: to retch is to heave as if being sick

explanation.surface: A sick wife is pitied as a poor devil.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an unfortunate, miserable person is a pitiable creature, a poor devil.

clue.text: Bring to bear and retry a terribly well-known job

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are handled badly, so the fodder before it is jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone retries a famous job and tries to apply pressure in doing so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' joins the two stretches of fodder; the letters of BRING TO BEAR plus RETRY A are rearranged. 'Job' in crime slang is a heist: the 1963 mail-train hold-up in Buckinghamshire is Britain's most famous one.
explanation.definitionFit: In criminal slang a job is a heist, and the 1963 mail-train raid is the most notorious British example.

clue.text: Tearful outside practice, try to turn back a best friend?

indicators.note: outside means the first word's letters wrap round the next word's

parts.note: someone tearful is sad
usage is customary practice

indicators.note: to turn back tells us the word for try is read in reverse

parts.note: to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: A tearful person tries to win back a best friend.
explanation.walkthrough: Dog is 'man's best friend', so the question mark flags a dachshund as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A dachshund, nicknamed for its long body, is a kind of dog, and dogs are proverbially man's best friend.

clue.text: One place to settle travelling circus — almost outside shopping centre

indicators.note: outside tells us the jumbled letters go around the next piece
travelling suggests movement, so the letters of the two words are shifted around

parts.note: a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: A touring circus nearly sets up outside a shopping centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' looks like an instruction to shorten, but it is anagram fodder alongside 'circus': their letters make SCLAIMSCOURT, with MALL put inside after the first S.
explanation.definitionFit: Minor civil disputes are settled in this low-level tribunal, so it is a venue for settling claims.

clue.text: Rose going topless gets prodded

indicators.note: going topless means the first letter of the word for rose is removed

parts.note: rose as in surged upwards

explanation.surface: A woman called Rose goes topless and is poked about.
explanation.walkthrough: Rose looks like a name or a flower, but it is the past tense of rise.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to prod someone is to push or urge them on.

clue.text: A soft cheese? No thanks — some fruit

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft

indicators.note: no thanks says the word for thanks is dropped from the cheese

parts.note: ricotta is a soft Italian cheese

explanation.surface: Offered a soft cheese, someone declines and takes some fruit instead.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British informal for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the stone fruit is one kind of fruit, related to the peach.

clue.text: Blokes in hospital department turning up for fundamental procedure?

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the whole is read from the bottom
in places the blokes inside the department

parts.note: A and E, accident and emergency, is a hospital department
blokes are men

explanation.surface: Men in a hospital department show up for a basic procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fundamental' plays on fundament, the buttocks: a rectal procedure. A&E is the British casualty department.
explanation.definitionFit: Punning definition: the fundament is the backside, so a procedure performed there is a rectal flush.

clue.text: Press endlessly going after good girl with weak feature

indicators.note: going after places the press piece after good and girl

parts.note: a lass is a girl

indicators.note: endlessly means the final letter of the word for press is cut

parts.note: jaws press or clamp, as the jaws of a vice do

explanation.surface: A girl presses someone endlessly and shows a weak spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxing term: a chin that cannot take a punch is a fighter's weak point.

clue.text: Bother about Spain beginning to analyse what it once spent

indicators.note: about means the nuisance word goes round the letter for Spain

parts.note: a pest is a bother, a nuisance
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter of analyse

explanation.surface: Someone frets over Spain while starting to analyse its past spending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers back to Spain, so the definition is Spain's old money.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain's former currency, replaced by the euro in 2002, was what the country used to spend.

clue.text: Shrub requiring exceptional drainage

indicators.note: exceptional suggests something out of the ordinary, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A garden plant needs very good drainage.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a fragrant white-flowered evergreen bush, one particular kind of shrub.

clue.text: Destroyed small mollusc, flattened at last

parts.note: the cuttle, or cuttlefish, is a mollusc

indicators.note: at last takes the final letter of flattened

explanation.surface: A little mollusc is crushed flat and done for.
explanation.definitionFit: To sink a ship deliberately or wreck a plan is to destroy it.

clue.text: See 3
Deport European team with luggage on vacation

parts.note: XI, eleven in Roman numerals, is a football or cricket team

indicators.note: on vacation means the middle of luggage is emptied out, leaving its ends

explanation.surface: A European side on holiday with their bags get sent home.
explanation.definitionFit: To banish someone from their country is to send them out of it, a synonym for deport.

clue.text: See 4 down
Rising English author with no time for Scandinavian one

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the letters read upwards
with no says the letter for time is dropped

parts.note: E. Nesbit wrote The Railway Children

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming English writer is passed over for a Nordic rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' looks like praise for the English author, but it reverses the letters. 'one' carries on 'author': a Scandinavian writer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian playwright of A Doll's House is a Scandinavian writer, the author implied by 'one'.

clue.text: Antagonise Liberal MP running English town

indicators.note: running suggests movement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Liberal MP campaigning in an English town provokes people.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the Warwickshire spa resort is a town in England.

clue.text: One entertained by mostly fat, small, porky narrators

indicators.note: entertained by means the one is held within the trimmed fat word
mostly means the last letter of lard is lost

parts.note: lard is pig fat
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone sits among the chubby little narrators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porky' is Cockney rhyming slang: pork pies = lies, so porky narrators tell porkies.
explanation.definitionFit: Through the rhyming slang, those telling porkies (pork pies, lies) are people who do not tell the truth.

clue.text: Getting up, say, about to flatten lizard

indicators.note: getting up in a down clue means the letters for say read upwards

parts.note: EG, for example, means say
C, circa, means about
to KO, knock out, is to flatten someone

explanation.surface: Someone rises and is about to squash a lizard.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the small sticky-footed reptile is a type of lizard.

clue.text: Board needing agreement from EU neighbours

parts.note: France and Germany are neighbours in the EU, and yes is oui in French and ja in German
France and Germany are neighbours in the EU, and yes is oui in French and ja in German

explanation.surface: A board needs consent from neighbouring European countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' looks like a committee, but it is a seance board.
explanation.definitionFit: The lettered seance board with a planchette is a board used to spell out spirit messages.

clue.text: Rushed to collect rubbish that's thrown away

indicators.note: to collect means the word for rushed takes the rubbish inside it

parts.note: sped means rushed
crap is slang for rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone rushed to gather up rubbish that had been thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something discarded or dumped as useless has been thrown away.

clue.text: Series about lawsuit that is self- sustaining once started

definitions.text: that is self- sustaining once started

parts.note: a chain is a series of linked events
RE means about, concerning
an action is a lawsuit

explanation.surface: A series about a lawsuit that keeps going by itself once begun.
explanation.definitionFit: A process in which each event triggers the next, as in nuclear fission, keeps itself going once initiated.

clue.text: See 3
Fear of unlimited pain stopping workforce

indicators.note: stopping means the trimmed pain word plugs the gap within the workforce letters

parts.note: HR, human resources, stands for the workforce

indicators.note: unlimited means the first and last letters are removed

parts.note: sorrow is emotional pain

explanation.surface: Dread that endless pain will halt the staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: intense fear or dread is terror.

clue.text: Incorporate muscle, getting brothers to retreat

parts.note: an ab is an abdominal muscle

indicators.note: to retreat means the brothers word goes backwards

explanation.surface: A bodybuilder takes on more muscle while the brothers back off.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something in and make it part of oneself is to incorporate it.

clue.text: Centrally allocated in pieces of eight

indicators.note: in pieces suggests something broken up, so those central letters are rearranged
centrally takes the central five letters of allocated

explanation.surface: Pirate's coins, pieces of eight, are shared out centrally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces of eight' looks like old Spanish coins, but 'in pieces' is the anagram signal, leaving 'of eight' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the number system with base eight is the meaning of the adjective.

clue.text: Calling by scene of shooting with a new opening

indicators.note: with a new opening says the first letter is changed to another

parts.note: a film is shot on location

explanation.surface: A film location gets a new entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shooting' suggests guns, but it is filming. The clue does not name the new first letter; the definition settles it as V.
explanation.definitionFit: A calling is a strong sense of suitability for a career, a synonym.

clue.text: Without introduction, approach rendezvous

indicators.note: without introduction means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: an avenue is a way of approach, a line of attack

explanation.surface: Without being introduced, someone walks up to a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A rendezvous is a meeting place, and a venue is where an event is held.

clue.text: See 4 down
Destroy ring with opening for tiny round gemstone

indicators.note: round means the assembled letters are turned around

parts.note: to zap is to destroy
O is ring-shaped

indicators.note: opening for takes the first letter of tiny

explanation.surface: Destroying a ring for a tiny round jewel.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the yellow precious stone is one gemstone.

clue.text: Manx cat, as it were, beside monument

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the cat loses its final letter

parts.note: a panther is a big cat
on can mean beside, as in a town on a river

explanation.surface: A tailless cat sits by a monument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as it were' admits that 'Manx' is borrowed from the tailless Isle of Man breed to mean cut off at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A temple to all the gods, or a building honouring the illustrious dead, is a monument.

clue.text: Judge, initially under pressure, in a fix

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of under
in puts the pressure letter inside the fix

parts.note: a fix, a predicament, is a mire

explanation.surface: A judge, pressured at first, finds himself in a difficult spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee who adjudicates a match, as in cricket, acts as its judge.

clue.text: Depression round recruit that's delaying mass battle action

indicators.note: round means the dent word goes around the rest

parts.note: a dent is a depression

indicators.note: delaying means the letter for mass comes later in the word

parts.note: to employ is to recruit

explanation.surface: A slump in recruitment is holding up an army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' reads as an economic slump, but here it is a physical hollow; 'delaying' means the mass letter arrives late in the recruit word.
explanation.definitionFit: The positioning of troops for combat is a military operation in battle.

clue.text: Zulu champion relinquishing crown for nothing

parts.note: Zulu is Z in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: relinquishing crown means the top letter is dropped

parts.note: a champion is a hero

explanation.surface: A Zulu champion gives up his title for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure nought represents nothing, a synonym.
